name: g2_electron
formula: Δa_e^lattice = 0 at this loop order (electron at N=0; threshold E_res = m_e·φ^11 ≈ 101.69 MeV; m_e ≪ E_res; N=11 threshold exponent Tier 3)
tier: Tier 3/4 activation-threshold hypothesis (in tension with QFT decoupling, Δa_e ~ 6×10⁻¹⁴; no Tier 2 support; threshold exponent N=11 Tier 3); α-input contingent
app_psc_precision_str: Cs-α: Δa_e = -1.01 × 10⁻¹² (3.9σ); Rb-α: Δa_e = +0.34 × 10⁻¹² (2.2σ); the null is in tension with both α inputs

extra.alpha_input_caveat: Cs-based α (Parker et al. 2018) gives Δa_e ≈ -1.01×10⁻¹² (3.9σ); Rb-based α (Morel et al. 2020) gives Δa_e ≈ +0.34×10⁻¹² (2.1σ), with a_e from Fan et al. 2023. The earlier 'Cs 0.96σ agreement / Rb 3.94σ tension' labels were swapped and are withdrawn. The Cs and Rb α values disagree with each other by 5.5σ, which keeps this row in PENDING-α-RESOLUTION until both α-input branches agree with the null prediction or the external α discord resolves. Binary gate: next-gen atom-interferometry α measurements (Rb-α2 / Cs-α2 / matter-wave gradiometry).
extra.interpretation: Under the Tier 3/4 activation-threshold hypothesis (not derived; in tension with QFT decoupling, Δa_e ~ 6×10⁻¹⁴) there is no activated lattice vertex correction for a_e at this loop order because the electron's rest mass (0.511 MeV) is well below the cage-depinning threshold E_res = m_e·φ^11 ≈ 101.69 MeV (safety factor ≈ φ^11 ≈ 199). Under the hypothesis only leptons at N ≥ 11 (muon N=11, tau N=17) would activate the geometric 1/5 phason vertex correction. The observed (a_e^exp − a_e^SM) gap is not consistent with zero within 2σ for either α input (3.9σ with Cs-α, 2.1σ with Rb-α), so the null is not supported at present; the row stays PENDING-α-RESOLUTION. Falsifier: any future measurement establishing |Δa_e^anom| > 10⁻¹² at >3σ robustly across α inputs would challenge the activation-threshold hypothesis.
